This name resonates deeply with those who hold Hindu beliefs and exemplifies the rich cultural heritage of India.

historical_references.reference: The name Deveshwar is derived from the Sanskrit words 'deva' meaning god and 'ishwar' meaning ruler or controller. It was a title given to various Hindu deities and temple lords throughout history.
historical_references.context: The name Deveshwar was used in Hindu scriptures and inscriptions to refer to Hindu gods and temple lords, emphasizing their divine and ruling status.

historical_references.reference: During the medieval period in India, the rulers of the Maratha Empire used the title Deveshwar as a part of their official titles to signify their divine status and authority over their kingdoms.
historical_references.context: The title Deveshwar was adopted by the Maratha rulers to emphasize their connection to the Hindu gods and their role as protectors of their people and territories.
